section-1.name: section 1
section-1.title: vesting clause - gives the legislative branch the powers listed in article 1

section-2.name: section 2
section-2.title: House of Representatives
content: each state gets a certain number of representatives in the house depending on the population
each state is guaranteed at least one representative
representatives must live in the state they are representing
representatives serve 2 year terms and the people vote for a representative for their district
the House is the closest part of government to the people - it is most subject to public opinion and swings in public sentiment
House has the power to impeach

section-3.name: section 3
section-3.title: Senate
content: 17th amendment gave the people the right to vote for their senators
the Senate is divided into 3 classes - so 1/3 of the senate is up for election every 2 years
senators must live in the state they are representing
the vice president presides over the senate
vice president does not vote unless a senate vote ties
is the house impeaches, the senate holds the impeachment hearing
if the impeachment involves the president of the United States, the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court presides over the impeachment hearing

section-4.name: section 4
section-4.title: Congress - the House of Representatives and the Senate together
content: time, place, and manner of elections
congress has to meet once a year - first monday of december unless they by law choose a different day

section-5.name: section 5
section-5.title: Proceedings and rules
content: gives the Senate and House of Reps. details of what exact authority they have within themselves
gives the Sente and House rules for keeping records and rules for their sessions (sessions is basically a way of saying their 'seasons')

section-6.name: section 6
section-6.title: rights and restrictions
content: terms for compensation/salary for Senate and House members
privileges from arrest unless there is treason, felony or breach of peace

section-7.name: section 7
section-7.title: rules for how congress can make laws
content: bills involving a raise in taxes must originate in the house - they can be amended by the Senate
role of the President in the passing of bills into law

section-8.name: section 8
section-8.title: enumerated/explicitly stated powers of Congress
content: coin money and regulate the value thereof
create all courts below the Supreme Court
make all laws necessary and proper to execute their enumerated powers
necessary and proper clause / elastic clause

section-9.name: section 9
section-9.title: Limitations to the power of Congress
content: Congress cannot ban the importation of slaves until 25 years after the Constitution is adopted - 1808
allowed Congress to place a tax on each person that was imported during this period, with the max being $10 per person or slave

section-10.name: section 10
section-10.title: Powers denied to the states
content: States cannot print their own money or create their own currency
states cannot form a treaty of alliance or confederation
states cannot give titles of nobility
states cannot pass bill of attainder or ex post facto laws
acts of states that need consent of congress

section-1.name: section 1
section-1.title: function and selection
content: president and vice president are elected to 4 year terms
president and vice president can only serve 2 terms max
president is elected through electoral college
the number of electoral votes is assigned to each state by the number of representatives that state has plus 2 for the senators
president must be a natural born U.S. citizen (born in the U.S.)
president has to take an oath of office

section-2.name: section 2
section-2.title: Powers
content: president is commander in chief of the army, navy, and state militas if called to service under the U.S.
president has the ability to pardon people convicted of crimes or cutting their sentence short - except in the case of impeachment
Getting advice and consent from the Senate
the president can appoint officials to the executive branch and the judicial branch but they must be confirmed by the Senate
the president can create treaties but a treaty must be ratified by 2/3's of the Senate

section-3.name: section 3
section-3.title: duties
content: president must give congress an update in a State of the Union Address from time to time in writing or in person

section-1.name: section
section-1.title: Vesting clause - gives the judiciary branch the powers in article 3
content: 1 supreme court with 8 associate justices and a chief justice
supreme courts and lower courts are empowered with Judicial Power
the marbury v. madison case said interpreted this judicial power as "judicial review"
judicial review means only the courts have power to interpret law and the constitution
Judicial review is the process that, in finding federal and state laws unconstitutional, makes such laws null and void.

The principle of judicial review was first established in 1803 with Marbury v. Madison, a U.S. Supreme Court case that found that parts of the Federal Judiciary Act of 1789 were inconsistent with Article III of the U.S. Constitution.

Civil Rights: The U.S. Supreme Court also takes an active role in protecting the rights of citizens, or “civil rights”. Civil rights are those rights of citizens that the federal and state governments have an affirmative obligation to protect. Civil rights are most often understood to include protecting equal protection and due process rights found in the Fourteenth Amendment, which also defines citizenship. The U.S. Supreme Court engages in statutory interpretation in civil rights cases. This means that the Court is interpreting the meaning of statutes, but does not evaluate those statutes for their constitutionality.
congress' power to establish article III (3) courts
congress' power to establish non article III (3) courts

section-2.name: section 2
section-2.title: defining limits to what cases Federal Courts can hear
content: supreme court has both original and appellete jurisdiction but most cases get to the supreme court through the appellete jurisdiction meaning the case has been appealed by a party to get a higher court to review a lower courts decision
cases where United States is one of the parties involved
states and citizens of other states

section-3.name: section 3
section-3.title: Treason
content: treason is the only explicitly stated crime in the constitution

section-1.name: section 1
section-1.title: full faith and credit clause
content: full faith credit clause says public acts and records of other states must be fully respected by other states
expanded the idea of federalism and what states owe to each other and what the federal government owes to the states
borrows language from articles of the confederation

section-3.name: section 3
section-3.title: new states and federal property
content: federal and state power over public lands
prohibits the formation of a new state that uses a part of a current state or combines 2 states, unless approved by both state legislatures in congress

section-4.name: section 4
section-4.title: republican form of government
content: a republican form of government is guaranteed for each state

section-1.name: section 1
section-1.title: Adding a new amendment to the constitution
content: states vote: 3/4 of state legislatures (or state ratifying conventions) must approve
if all votes pass the amendment is ratified (accepted/officically added to constitution)
2/3 of states must approve to propose amendment
congress would hold a national convention to discuss proposal
states vote: 3/4 of state legislatures (or state ratifying conventions) must approve
if all requirements are met, amendment is ratified (accepted/officially added to constitution)
this method has never been used
unamendable subjects ("No state, without its consent, shall be deprived of its equal suffrage in the Senate" - introduced by Roger Sherman)

section-1.name: section 1
section-1.title: Supreme law of the land
content: debts that belonged to the U.S. under the articles of confederation were taken on by the U.S. under the new federal government under the constitution

section-1.name: section 1
section-1.title: requirements
content: 9 states must approve the constitution to ratify it
